result.title: When Does Causality Help in Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection?
result.summary: Causality-aware scoring is common in multivariate time-series anomaly detection, yet the literature rarely states when it helps. Holding one causality-guided autoencoder (DeCauAE) fixed, we vary graph quality, anomaly type and protocol against ground truth. Graph quality fixes the payoff: on a twenty-variable DAG the gain over a graph-free autoencoder decays as the graph is corrupted. Anomaly type fixes the target: the structural factor lifts window F1 from 0.800 to 0.976 where anomalies break conditional structure, and its advantage vanishes below a break severity s 0.3. Protocol fixes the ranking: point-adjusted F1 lets a random score match the full model, while range-aware VUS separates the autoencoder family from the classical baselines. On real benchmarks the causal module pays only where density makes a system eligible and cross-subsample reproducibility selects entities inside it; enabling it everywhere costs 0.012 VUS-ROC. The structural factor also transfers to classical detectors .

AI.brief_summary: 固定一个因果引导自编码器，系统改变图质量、异常类型与评测协议，考察因果评分在何种条件下才带来增益，并给出仅在合格系统上启用因果模块的选择准则。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「结构先验的收益取决于数据条件与协议、并按资格门控启用模块」的诊断思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据或结构约束何时真正起作用、以及评价指标对结论的影响；领域为多变量时间序列异常检测，迁移需自行判断。
